quest.title: A Thorough Investigation
quest.description: Ilyas remembered two things that he had to do, one of which is to collect his pay at the Research Preparation Center.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x550, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

talks.objective: Head towards the Research Preparation Center
Talk with the staff at the Research Preparation Center

dialogues.speaker: Makesh
dialogues.text: Acting Grand Sage Alhaitham, I've sent this period's research expenses report to your office. Have you taken a look? Are there any issues with it?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I did. Recent research expenses have decreased quite a bit compared to past figures.

dialogues.speaker: Makesh
dialogues.text: Yes, though that is primarily because there are fewer scholars with research needs.

dialogues.speaker: Makesh
dialogues.text: But that can be a rather... convoluted topic. Might I ask why you are here today?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I believe you know this individual — his name is Ilyas. He worked part-time here, and he's here for his paycheck.

dialogues.speaker: Makesh
dialogues.text: Oh, yes, of course, though... Ilyas, where have you been these past few days?

dialogues.speaker: Makesh
dialogues.text: That was our busy period, but then you disappeared without a word. Everyone had to pick up the slack.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, something unexpected came up...

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: But I know I've caused trouble for everyone... Is there anything I can do to make up for it?

dialogues.speaker: Makesh
dialogues.text: The other researchers have more or less finished your share of the work. However, there is one thing that has yet to be settled.

dialogues.speaker: Makesh
dialogues.text: Do you remember Chandra? You were in charge of following up on his off-site research application.

dialogues.speaker: Makesh
dialogues.text: He retracted his application a few days ago and canceled his off-site project.

dialogues.speaker: Makesh
dialogues.text: He's the twelfth person to retract a research application this month. I'd like you to ask him why he did that. Chandra is probably having coffee at this hour, so you can find him at the cafe.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Understood. Then, about my paycheck...

dialogues.speaker: Makesh
dialogues.text: I'll pay you in full once you return. However, make sure you don't disappear without saying anything again. Be considerate to your colleagues and give them some forewarning at least.

dialogues.speaker: Makesh
dialogues.text: Is this acceptable, Acting Grand Sage Alhaitham?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I have no objections.

dialogues.speaker: Chandra
dialogues.text: Ilyas? Long time no see. What can I do for you?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: I heard that you canceled your research project, so I'm just here to ask you why.

dialogues.speaker: Chandra
dialogues.text: Oh, that... Erm, it's really nothing special. I just don't feel like going anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Chandra
dialogues.text: I'm not the only one who canceled, right? I mean, people have had no motivation to conduct research lately, haven't they?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: "No motivation to conduct research"?

dialogues.speaker: Chandra
dialogues.text: Yeah... Say, who might you be? You look sort of familiar.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Oh, don't mind me. Please continue.

dialogues.speaker: Chandra
dialogues.text: Well, with the downfall of the sages not long ago, many of the projects that they led were put on hold while they were being investigated.

dialogues.speaker: Chandra
dialogues.text: With the situation being so volatile, people are picking up random things to do to kill time. No one wants to risk starting any new research until it's clear how things will pan out in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: When you say "how things will pan out," you actually mean "what the new sages would have interest in," right?

dialogues.speaker: Chandra
dialogues.text: Wow, talk about blunt... But that isn't the only reason for the lack of motivation to start new research.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what are the other reasons?

dialogues.speaker: Chandra
dialogues.text: Well... because the Akasha Terminal shut down.

dialogues.speaker: Chandra
dialogues.text: I'm sure you're all aware that we require all kinds of knowledge to perform any of the research we do.

dialogues.speaker: Chandra
dialogues.text: Back then, the Akasha would respond to any of our requests for the knowledge we needed.

dialogues.speaker: Chandra
dialogues.text: It was beyond convenient. We didn't have to spend an extended amount of time studying, so we were able to immediately run various tests and experiments.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I see.

dialogues.speaker: Chandra
dialogues.text: You get it, right? After having had a taste of something so amazing, who can be bothered to manually sift through data and files ever again?

dialogues.speaker: Chandra
dialogues.text: There are only a handful of people at the Akademiya who are starting new projects or performing research. Most people are like me, waiting for a recognized researcher to start a project before immediately applying to join.

dialogues.speaker: Chandra
dialogues.text: Although our names will be further down in the paper, we'll have a much easier time. We don't have to do most of the mental heavy-lifting — all we have to do is focus on our assigned tasks.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Ugh!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ilyas, what's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: My head... It hurts...

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: I remember now... I remember what Siraj said to me as he approached...

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: "You will become 'Siraj Number 36.' Fuse yourself with a consciousness under my control. Think only in accordance with a set module... like a worker bee in a beehive."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't get it. What does that even mean?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It's what Siraj was researching, and the topic of the thesis he had submitted: "collective consciousness and the path of evolution."

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Siraj believed that by achieving three objectives, he could create a collective consciousness in human society and drive humans toward their ultimate evolution.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: First, he would rank test subjects in descending order of ability, with number one serving as the "Overmind."

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: This Overmind would then divide tasks into numerous modules and delegate them to the collective's members, based on their assigned number and the task's importance.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Lastly, this system must support the rapid exchange of information within the collective, or even better, allow its members to share their memories and emotions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon still doesn't get it. What's the point of all that?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Think of it as linking many minds together and tailoring a given mind's assigned work based on its compatibility.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Eventually, everyone's minds will be consolidated into a new form of existence that is both an "individual" and an "organization."

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Siraj believes this "collective consciousness" is superior to individual humans.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, squishing a whole bunch of people together... Paimon thinks that sounds horrible.

response.speaker: Ilyas
response.text: It's just as Alhaitham said. Siraj gave all the test subjects different numbers. Bigger numbers meant you had a lower rank, so your assigned tasks were less complex, such as being responsible for everyone's basic needs.

response.speaker: Ilyas
response.text: Smaller numbers were ranked higher, so you'd be given more complex assignments, like planning for the future. Siraj referred to me as Number 36. And I think that was a low-ranking number.

response.speaker: Ilyas
response.text: I also recall that Siraj said his plan was proceeding very quickly, and that the "Hive" would soon be complete.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh no, then we gotta hurry! We have to stop him before it's complete!

response.speaker: Ilyas
response.text: I tried my best, but that's all I can remember. I still can't recall where the cave is. I'm really sorry...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Take your time. You'll eventually remember it all. However, something doesn't seem right. Some details don't add up...

response.speaker: Ilyas
response.text: What's off?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: You were only designated as number 36? What a shame. From what I can see, your talents merit a smaller number.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I'm not sure what Siraj's numbering system is based on... Anyway, we're done here. Let's go.

response.speaker: Chandra
response.text: Please, wait!

response.speaker: Chandra
response.text: I heard you all talking about Siraj just now. Are you looking for him?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Hm? Do you know something?

response.speaker: Chandra
response.text: Well, Siraj is pretty popular as of late. I heard he's gained recognition from a lot of well-known researchers. Supposedly, he's a strong contender for being one of the next sages.

response.speaker: Chandra
response.text: There are many who would give up everything to be a part of his research team. I'm nothing special, though, so I doubt I'd get the opportunity...

response.speaker: Chandra
response.text: That said, I do know a researcher who received an invitation from Siraj but declined it. Her name is Janaki.

response.speaker: Chandra
response.text: If you're interested, you can try to find her. She's usually reading at the pavilion in the garden.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you Janaki? We'd like to ask you a couple of things about Siraj!

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: Ilyas?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Do you know me? I'm sorry, but I don't recognize you...

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: Are you playing dumb with me?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: No, I'm not! I actually have amnesia, so I've lost a lot of my memories.

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: And? Are you trying to say that I should forgive you just because you've forgotten what you've done?

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: Or are you using the Acting Grand Sage as backup to settle things with me? The two biggest "loners" teaming up... What a terrible thought...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That's enough. There seems to be a dispute between the two of you, but I have no interest in that.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I heard that Siraj once invited you to join his project. Is that true?

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: ...So what if it is?

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: Siraj did extend an invitation to me, and I was also interested in his project.

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: I think it was about collective consciousness or something. Anyway, he said that I could be Number 45. I refused because I thought that rank was too low.

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: No one wants to be placed at the bottom, certainly not me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ilyas is Number 36 and Janaki was supposed to be Number 45... Just how many people did Siraj have his eyes on?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Tell me, did Siraj tell you how he assigned numbers?

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: Yeah. Remember how the sages took advantage of the Akasha and extracted Jnana Energy from our heads back then?

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: They left a document that records the amount of Jnana Energy that the Akasha had extracted from each person.

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: I don't know how Siraj got his hands on that document, but he used it as the basis for his numbering system.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Hmm, I see. He believes that this data can be used to evaluate a person's computing power...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is it true, though?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Putting aside the validity of the data, it is meaningless to judge individuals based solely on their Jnana Energy.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: At most, Jnana Energy can only be seen as representing a portion of a person's abilities. Humans are complicated beings, so it is impossible to evaluate them using a single criterion.

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: See? I knew I couldn't have only been ranked as 45.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: What else do you know about Siraj?

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: That's it. He came to me, I refused, and that was the end of it.

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: Is there anything else you needed? If not, I'm outta here. I've had enough of this eyesore.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Please, wait. I... I still want to know what I did in the past.

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: You really forgot?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: I swear I don't remember anything.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can vouch for him! The matra also said that he's truly lost his memories.

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: I see. You know what? It's better this way.

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: I get angry just thinking about it, so I really don't have the patience to fill you in. All you need to know is that you got a lot of people in trouble back then, including me.

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: That's all that I have to say. Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And she's gone... She doesn't seem to like you very much. Do you really not remember anything?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: I really don't, but after she said that, I've had this heavy feeling in my chest.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: I guess... I did something really horrible...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Do you want to remember?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Even though you're a witness against Siraj in this case, you've also lost your memory.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: No one can force you to remember if you don't want to. Even if you managed to remember, all you would need to do is feign ignorance and tell us that you tried the best you could, but to no avail.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: I'm not sure what to do... Like I said before, for some reason, I felt a sense of freedom when I realized I had lost my memories...

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: But I feel like I shouldn't be allowed to go free so easily. I still want to remember everything. What should I do?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I can look up your file.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Something that "caused trouble for a lot of people" in the past must be on file somewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Would you like me to look into it?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: ...Yes, please.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Alright, then let's return to the House of Daena. We've spent enough time here, and you should go and get your paycheck.

talks.objective: Search for information related to Ilyas

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Let's split up for now. Ilyas, you go and deal with that. The rest of you, come to the archives with me.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: We'll meet back here later and then head over to Gandharva Ville.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Okay... Thank you all so much.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Relax, Ilyas. Being nervous accomplishes nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: That's true... *sigh* I'm ready. No matter what I've done, I'm ready to face it.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: I'll also try my best to remember anything else related to Siraj. We'll put an end to all of this.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I'm holding you to that. See you later.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Okay, the important files from the last few years should all be here.

talks.objective: Wait for Alhaitham to look through the information

dialogues.speaker: About the Corps of Thirty Application Fee
dialogues.text: "There are many vacancies for sages, and the number of suspicious people spreading various news in Sumeru City has increased significantly recently. The Corps of Thirty are looking to recruit for surveillance to ensure the city's peace and stability..."

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: ...Hmm.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Nothing. Anyway, I found Ilyas's file. Let's meet downstairs.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: What... have I done?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: This file indicates that you were once commended by the Akademiya for your "courage and sense of justice." You were considered a "hero."

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Huh? Me?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Yes. Your instructor was engaging in academic fraud, and you were the one who reported him.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Your report was found to be true after a series of investigations, and your instructor was brought to justice by the matra.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: This incident caused quite the commotion, and the Akademiya sent you a commendation.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Ugh!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: What is it? Are any memories coming back to you?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: No, it's just... My head feels like it's being ripped apart again... It hurts...

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Did I seriously do that? Then why...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Let's put this matter aside for now. It isn't directly related to Siraj, so there's no need to push yourself over it.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: ...I'm sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: That should have been something good to hear, but my body is instinctively rejecting it. I feel like I'll black out if I try to remember...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Take it slow. Recovering memories is no easy task, especially when it involves memories that you don't want to remember.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Just do what you think is right.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Thank you. I'm not sure how you're so calm and composed all the time, but it does make me feel more confident about the situation I'm in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's head to Gandharva Ville and deliver Ilyas's paycheck to his sister! Come on!

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: We should be close. Let me think... It should be this way.

dialogues.speaker: Alyasa
dialogues.text: Ilyas? What are you doing back here?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Dad... It's nothing. I was just wondering how everyone was doing.

dialogues.speaker: Ashera
dialogues.text: You sure everything's okay? Did they bully you again? It's alright, you can tell us...

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Ugh!

dialogues.speaker: Ashera
dialogues.text: Ilyas! What's wrong!?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: I'm fine, just a minor headache. I haven't been getting much rest lately...

dialogues.speaker: Alyasa
dialogues.text: *sigh* Back then, I told you not to be a hero. Look how things turned out.

dialogues.speaker: Alyasa
dialogues.text: I can't imagine how things are going for you at the Akademiya. We've even been receiving threat letters.

dialogues.speaker: Ashera
dialogues.text: You don't have to force yourself to stay at the Akademiya. You can always come back home...

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: I'm alright, I just need a little rest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ilyas doesn't seem like he wants them to know that he has amnesia...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He doesn't want his family to worry.

dialogues.speaker: Izebel
dialogues.text: Hey, hey, that's enough, you two. Ilyas isn't feeling well. You can keep nagging him once we get home.

dialogues.speaker: Izebel
dialogues.text: Ilyas, let's find somewhere to talk.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Ilyas's sister brings you to a quieter place.

dialogues.speaker: Izebel
dialogues.text: So, how's your headache?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: It's much better now. Oh, here — it's this month's paycheck. How's everything at home?

dialogues.speaker: Izebel
dialogues.text: Same old, same old... It's just that everyone's worried about you.

dialogues.speaker: Izebel
dialogues.text: Don't mind their nagging. Deep down, they know that you did the right thing.

dialogues.speaker: Izebel
dialogues.text: It's just that after hearing a lot of bad rumors about you, and seeing all the threatening letters... Well, they're Mom and Dad. Maybe they just want you to... conform a bit more.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: "Conform"...

dialogues.speaker: Izebel
dialogues.text: Yeah, you don't remember? After the incident, you...

dialogues.speaker: Izebel
dialogues.text: Ilyas? What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Ah... I see. I remember now. Don't worry, I remember now.

dialogues.speaker: Izebel
dialogues.text: You're acting a little weird today, you know? Anyway, I understand your decision, but Mom, Dad, and I just want you to be happy.

dialogues.speaker: Izebel
dialogues.text: I don't care if you're a hero or not. I just want you to enjoy life and relax more.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Your understanding is a great comfort to him.

dialogues.speaker: Izebel
dialogues.text: Is it? That's good. Are you a friend of his?

dialogues.speaker: Izebel
dialogues.text: Huh... Wait a moment... you look familiar. Have you visited Gandharva Ville before?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: #More so these two. My name is Alhaitham, and this is {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Izebel
dialogues.text: Oh, that rings a bell... At any rate, I feel more at ease knowing that my brother has friends.

dialogues.speaker: Izebel
dialogues.text: Would you like to join us for dinner? I just happened to buy some extra food.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Sorry, but I still have things I need to take care of.

dialogues.speaker: Izebel
dialogues.text: Well, that's a shame... Okay, I'll get going then. Take care of yourself, Ilyas!

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I won't do anything to make you guys worry again.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You remember now?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Yes, I do.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Thanks for that. You know, you don't seem like such a bad person.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Is that your way of conveying gratitude?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Oh, my apologies... but I meant every word. Remember when I asked at the tavern if we had ever met?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: I said there was a sense of familiarity, but what I really meant was a sense of loathing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Loathing?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Yeah, but having spent some time with you, I realized that you're not someone I'd dislike to that extent.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Strange, isn't it? Why did I have those thoughts at that time?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: My strength is that I don't care about what others think. If you could also develop this quality, then you won't be as bothered by complicated social relationships.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: It'd be great if I could think like you. Ah, but first things first, I remember where Siraj's cave is now. I'll take you there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? That's great!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh, Paimon remembers that you said there were two things that you had to do. We've only checked off one, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What about the other one? Are we not gonna do that first?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: There are more important things at hand... We have to stop Siraj before he completes his collective consciousness, or it'll be too late.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're right. Let's head out!

dialogues.speaker: Makesh
dialogues.text: Things at the Akademiya have been strange lately. People have become much less interested in doing research.

dialogues.speaker: Makesh
dialogues.text: This will definitely be bad in the long run...

dialogues.speaker: Chandra
dialogues.text: Hmm? What can I do for you?

dialogues.speaker: Makesh
dialogues.text: Here's your paycheck. Next time, remember to give us a heads-up if you'll be absent.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Got it. Thank you so much.

dialogues.speaker: Makesh
dialogues.text: No problem. Let me know if you ever run into any trouble.

dialogues.speaker: About the Sleepwalking Eccentric
dialogues.text: "The Rtawahist Darshan has also had an abundance of weirdos. Recently, there is a new rumor that a student has the ability to write 'the Heaven-Sent Thesis.' The circumstances are still under investigation..."

dialogues.speaker: About the "Ghost of Pardis Dhyai"
dialogues.text: "There are witnesses that say that there is a mysterious shadow wandering around Pardis Dhyai at night. The investigation found nothing suspicious and the case was closed."

dialogues.speaker: About recent developments in Pardis Dhyai
dialogues.text: "Pardis Dhyai has been peaceful recently, and there's nothing out of the ordinary."

dialogues.speaker: Makesh
dialogues.text: (Well, seeing as it's Acting Grand Sage Alhaitham...)

dialogues.speaker: Chandra
dialogues.text: (The coffee is really bitter today...)

dialogues.speaker: Chandra
dialogues.text: (*sigh* I wish I could've joined Siraj's research project, too...)

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: (I can buy my sister a new dress...)

dialogues.speaker: Makesh
dialogues.text: (What is Ilyas's relation to Acting Grand Sage Alhaitham?)

dialogues.speaker: Makesh
dialogues.text: (There's just too much to do...)

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: (Did I pay too much for that piece of jewelry today?)
